resolution: SIMPLE PATH (coordinator-authorized fallback after the comment-aware lexer approach failed its 4th review round). Root cause: ci/checks/agent-instruction-runtime-dormant.sh (FF-COMP-6, comment-BLIND grep) flagged two pure documentation comments in the non-allowlisted src/http/agents.ts that named 'the agent-instruction promote path' in prose (byte-identical to origin/dev; zero code-level reads), so npm run fitness was red on clean dev, masking the honest signal on every branch. FIX: reword those two comments so they no longer contain the literal token ('the agent-instruction promote path' -> 'the instruction-promote path in artifacts.ts'), and keep the gate comment-blind (reverted byte-identical to BASE). This has ZERO false-negative surface: the comment-blind gate can never hide a real agent_instruction read (there is no comment lexer to evade), so R1/R2/R3 and any future R-N are structurally impossible. The only 'cost' — flagging comment mentions of the literal — is eliminated at the source by not writing the token in prose.
diff_vs_base: git diff b50308be: src/http/agents.ts = 4 comment lines changed (2 reworded pairs, comment-only, meaning preserved); docs only. ci/checks/agent-instruction-runtime-dormant.sh, ci/checks/data/frozen-sanctions.jsonl, docs/design/T-0152-security-invariants-catalog.md are ALL byte-identical to BASE (git diff b50308be on each is empty) — the abandoned comment-aware gate change, its auto_additive frozen-sanction, and its catalog family §7.8 were fully reverted.
why_simple_path: The comment-aware detector was reworked three times (R1 leading same-line block comment; R2 line-leading TS #private-field declaration; R3 regex-literal raw /*). Each revision the reviewer live-reproduced a NEW false-negative evasion of the same class. For R3 the reviewer proposed a general 'unterminated /* = not a comment' rule; I tested it empirically in scratch and it does NOT close the class — a regex /* followed by any later real /* */ block comment (ubiquitous trailing file note) still swallows the code between them (required R3 probe passes, but the regex+later-*/ residual returns hits=0). Closing that needs true regex-vs-division lexing, explicitly out of bounds. This tripped the coordinator's pre-set boundary ('if the unterminated fix does not close a swallow path, STOP and switch to the simple path'), so I pivoted. A comment-aware detector is the wrong tool for a security gate: every lexer gap is a place a real read can hide. Comment-blind + reworded comments = zero false negatives AND zero false positives.

friction_events: The comment-aware detector approach (R1/R2/R3) was a hand-rolled comment lexer in awk; each review round the reviewer found a new evasion shape of the same 'lexer mis-tokenizes -> false negative' class. LESSON: a comment-aware filter is the wrong posture for a security detector — a lexer gap hides a real violation. The robust fix is to keep the detector maximally strict (comment-blind, zero false-negative surface) and remove the false-positive trigger at its source (the literal token in a documentation comment). Pivoted to this on the coordinator's pre-authorized boundary.

Verified the residual swallow of the reviewer's proposed unterminated-/* rule in scratch BEFORE committing to it, which is what justified the pivot rather than shipping a 4th lexer revision with a known hole.
